name: Lymphatic Resonance Injector LRI-5 'Floodgate'
description:
The LRI-5 operates by firing a near-invisible pressurized micro-needle capable of penetrating standard dermal armor at ranges up to twelve meters. Upon subcutaneous delivery, the payload — a proprietary synthetic lymphotropic compound — binds to the target's lymphatic vessels and triggers a rapid cascading inflammatory response. The victim's own immune system becomes the instrument of incapacitation, producing systemic edema, joint failure, and acute respiratory distress within ninety seconds of exposure.

What distinguishes the Floodgate from conventional chemical delivery systems is its integration of piezoelectric disruption circuitry within the needle itself. As the micro-needle penetrates tissue, a brief localized vibration pulse fragments the tip into a mesh of sub-millimeter barbs, anchoring the delivery mechanism and ensuring full compound release even if the target attempts to remove it. This makes post-incident medical intervention significantly more complex and time-consuming.

The weapon's external profile is nearly indistinguishable from a high-end medical auto-injector — a deliberate design choice by Lazarus Pharmaceuticals, whose pharmaceutical division ostensibly produced the chassis for 'field triage applications.' Its plausible deniability as medical equipment has made it a favorite of corporate intelligence operatives and high-society assassins who operate in environments where weapons screening is routine.
specifications:
effective range: 0–12 meters
payload capacity: 6 doses per magazine
needle diameter: 0.3mm tungsten-ceramic composite
onset time: 60–90 seconds post-injection
weight: 0.4 kg loaded
dimensions: 18cm x 3cm x 2cm
power source: Micro-cell battery, 40 charges
reload time: 4 seconds (magazine swap)
tactical_use: Operators favor the Floodgate in close-access operations where loud weapons are counterproductive. It is typically deployed in social infiltration scenarios — a handshake, a crowded elevator, a brushing contact in a corridor. The ninety-second delay between injection and incapacitation gives the operator time to establish distance and alibi. Field doctrine recommends pairing deployment with an exit route, as incapacitated targets attract attention. Some operators use it as a non-lethal control tool by using half-doses, which produce debilitating pain without full systemic collapse.
cultural_context: The Floodgate occupies an unspoken tier of violence in GLMZ — the kind that leaves no visible wound and no obvious weapon. In corporate circles, being 'flooded' is understood as an unmistakable message: someone with access and patience wanted you down, not dead. This restraint is often more terrifying than outright assassination. Street operators who carry the LRI-5 are typically regarded with wariness even by peers, as its use implies a willingness to engage in prolonged, calculated cruelty rather than the swift violence most underworld actors prefer.
known_users: Yeva Sorokina (alleged — three unsolved boardroom collapses)
story_hooks: A prominent city councilor collapses during a televised session — no projectile, no poison detected in standard tox screens. The players are hired to find out how.
A black-market Floodgate surfaces in a neighborhood clinic, disguised in a legitimate medical kit. Someone is about to use it — but on whom?
Lazarus Pharmaceuticals quietly hires a team to recover all units from a stolen shipment before a regulatory audit traces the serial numbers back to their R&D division.
A player character is injected during a crowd scene and has ninety seconds to find a medical bay — or improvise.
